thread:
incident-bot: Pager: High token-count/billing spike detected for tenant T-8421 (customer: Orion Analytics) on Dedicated pool eu-west-2-ded. Token rate = 6.1x baseline, billing alerts firing. SLA hit risk. Paging on-call.

 dmitri: taking this — oncall handoff accepted (rot-3). paging details?

 incident-bot: Acknowledged by dmitri. Incident ID INC-1769123456. Alerts: billing-alert, token-usage, quota-exceeded.

 sara: customer contacted CS earlier reporting a sudden cost jump. traffic volume unchanged per their report. they asked us to investigate ASAP. cc: @emily for billing comms.

 lee: pulled a few raw request payloads from the ingest gateway: median tokens/request jumped from ~120 -> ~980 starting ~1769123200. sample looks like a blob with lots of nulls and surrogate pairs. suspect encoding mismatch.

 juniper: this reads like an encoding/tokenizer mismatch rather than malicious traffic. customer SDK maybe sending UTF-16 or sending JSON with escaped chars. if tokenizer treats it as byte-level it's exploding token counts.

 emily: tagging billing & CS — we should consider temporary credit and message template. Holding until we confirm root cause.

 dmitri: can someone paste a sample and a quick local tokenization run? I want to reproduce with our tokenizer binary.

 lee: grabbing a redacted sample now. saving to /tmp/t8421-sample.txt. running quick check:

 ```bash
 # in worker container
 file /tmp/t8421-sample.txt
 iconv -f utf-16 -t utf-8 /tmp/t8421-sample.txt > /tmp/t8421-utf8.txt || true
 python - <<'PY'
 from tokenizers import Tokenizer
 sample = open('/tmp/t8421-utf8.txt','rb').read()
 t = Tokenizer.from_file('/opt/tokenizers/byte_level.json')
 print('tokens (byte-level):', len(t.encode(sample.decode('utf-8',errors='ignore')).ids))
 PY
 ```

 lee: result: byte-level tokenizer shows ~950 tokens; but if I treat file as utf-16 and normalize to utf-8 first, tokens drop back to ~130. so definitely a UTF-16 payload hitting our byte-level path.

 juniper: root cause hypothesis: their ingestion client is sending UTF-16LE without the BOM, gateway doesn't auto-detect and we treat it as bytes, then byte-level tokenizer runs and counts each 2-byte sequence as separate tokens.

 marta: mitigation proposals (short term):
 - tenant-level request normalization: force decode in gateway with error handling and downconvert utf-16 -> utf-8 if detected.
 - temporary soft token cap for T-8421 (2000 tokens/request) returning 429 with friendly message & support link.
 - apply a proxy-level preprocessor that strips null bytes and common BOM patterns.

 dmitri: I'm going to push a hotfix to the gateway for normalization as a canary to a subset of the dedicated pool (eu-west-2-ded, shard-7). will coordinate deploy window. Juniper you'll have rollback?

 juniper: yes, I'll keep the revert ready. applying normalization is low-risk (decode-ignore) but we'll monitor tail latencies.

 emily: I'll draft a customer-safe message: "We're investigating an encoding issue that inflated token counts; temporary protections will be applied to avoid further unexpected billing. We'll follow-up with credits if appropriate." Pinged CS to review.

 lee: added a quick log rule to surface 0x00-heavy payloads and UTF-16 patterns so we can detect other tenants with same issue. dashboards updated.

 marta: I've set a temporary billing throttle on T-8421 via rate-limit policy (soft cap 2000 tokens/req, global per-tenant token budget reduced by 30%). Ops: visible in console under Dedicated -> Pools -> eu-west-2-ded -> Tenants.

 dmitri: deploying gateway normalization to canary shard now. command:

 ```bash
 deployctl canary --service=gateway --pool=eu-west-2-ded --shard=7 --image=gateway:v1.34.2-hotfix-encoding
 ```

 dmitri: canary logs show normalization applied. first 3000 requests normalized; token rates dropped to baseline for those. rolling to other shards over next 15m.

 juniper: watching metrics. no regression in latency so far. keeping rollback option.

 incident-bot: Update: severity lowered to SEV-2 based on mitigation. Incident remains open for postmortem and customer follow-up.

 emily: CS will propose a one-off billing credit for the affected invoice and ask customer to update their SDK/ingest settings. I'll include suggested text and diagnostics.

 lee: plan for medium-term: add encoding sniff in the gateway (UTF-16LE/BE detection via heuristics) + unit tests that include surrogate-heavy inputs. also add automatic normalization flag per-tenant toggle in console. adding ticket INFRA-3427.

 marta: created billing ticket BILL-9876 to track credits & finance sign-off. tagged with INC-1769123456.

 dmitri: timeline: canary -> full rollout complete by +30m, monitor 2h. then schedule a patch for tokenization library to handle these cases more gracefully next week.

 sara: thanks all — Emily/CS will lead customer comms. Ops team to keep monitoring and follow up with postmortem. will update status page if any external impact.

 incident-bot: Incident INC-1769123456 — status: mitigated (hotfix applied, tenant soft-cap active). Closing page in 2h pending stable metrics.

 dmitri: logging action items in the incident doc and assigning owners. I'll run a quick handoff to the on-call at rotation end. :wave:
